claim: A novel mouse plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) lineage is derived from the common lymphoid progenitors (CLPs).
source: We identified a novel mouse plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) lineage derived from the common lymphoid progenitors (CLPs) that is dependent on expression of Bcl11a.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript including conditional deletion experiments and lineage tracing.

claim: CLP-derived pDCs are dependent on expression of Bcl11a.
source: We identified a novel mouse plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) lineage derived from the common lymphoid progenitors (CLPs) that is dependent on expression of Bcl11a.
evidence: The abstract states this dependency, which is demonstrated through conditional deletion experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: CLP-derived pDCs are referred to as 'B-pDCs'.
source: These CLP-derived pDCs, which we refer to as 'B-pDCs', have a unique gene expression profile that includes hallmark B cell genes, normally not expressed in conventional pDCs.
evidence: The authors explicitly define their nomenclature for this cell population in the abstract.

claim: B-pDCs have a unique gene expression profile that includes hallmark B cell genes normally not expressed in conventional pDCs.
source: These CLP-derived pDCs, which we refer to as 'B-pDCs', have a unique gene expression profile that includes hallmark B cell genes, normally not expressed in conventional pDCs.
evidence: RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3 demonstrates differential gene expression between B-pDCs and conventional pDCs.

claim: B-pDCs express most classical pDC markers such as SIGLEC-H and PDCA1.
source: Despite expressing most classical pDC markers such as SIGLEC-H and PDCA1, B-pDCs lack IFN-α secretion, exhibiting a distinct inflammatory profile.
evidence: Flow cytometry data in Figures 1 and 2 show B-pDCs are gated as B220+ PDCA1+ cells, and imaging flow cytometry in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 confirms SIGLEC-H expression.

claim: B-pDCs lack IFN-α secretion.
source: Despite expressing most classical pDC markers such as SIGLEC-H and PDCA1, B-pDCs lack IFN-α secretion, exhibiting a distinct inflammatory profile.
evidence: ELISA data in Figure 2H shows IFN-α production is almost negligible in B-pDCs compared to conventional pDCs.

claim: B-pDCs exhibit a distinct inflammatory profile.
source: Despite expressing most classical pDC markers such as SIGLEC-H and PDCA1, B-pDCs lack IFN-α secretion, exhibiting a distinct inflammatory profile.
evidence: Gene expression analysis and functional assays (Figures 2 and 3) demonstrate elevated inflammatory markers and IL-12p40 production.

claim: B-pDCs induce T cell proliferation more robustly than canonical pDCs following Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) engagement.
source: Functionally, B-pDCs induce T cell proliferation more robustly than canonical pDCs following Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) engagement.
evidence: Co-culture experiments shown in Figure 2I and J demonstrate significantly higher percentages of CFSE-negative CD3+ T cells when cultured with B-pDCs compared to conventional pDCs.

claim: B-pDCs display elevated levels of the cell surface receptor tyrosine kinase AXL.
source: B-pDCs, along with another homogeneous subpopulation of myeloid-derived pDCs, display elevated levels of the cell surface receptor tyrosine kinase AXL, mirroring human AXL+ transitional DCs in function and transcriptional profile.
evidence: Imaging flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 shows ~60% of B-pDCs are positive for AXL, and RNA-seq data shows elevated Axl expression.

claim: A homogeneous subpopulation of myeloid-derived pDCs displays elevated levels of AXL.
source: B-pDCs, along with another homogeneous subpopulation of myeloid-derived pDCs, display elevated levels of the cell surface receptor tyrosine kinase AXL, mirroring human AXL+ transitional DCs in function and transcriptional profile.
evidence: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis in Figure 5 identifies pDC5 as an Axl+ myeloid-derived pDC population.

claim: Murine B-pDCs mirror human AXL+ transitional DCs in function and transcriptional profile.
source: B-pDCs, along with another homogeneous subpopulation of myeloid-derived pDCs, display elevated levels of the cell surface receptor tyrosine kinase AXL, mirroring human AXL+ transitional DCs in function and transcriptional profile.
evidence: Gene expression analysis shows B-pDCs express markers associated with human AXL+ DCs (AXL, CD81, CD86, LYZ2), and functional assays demonstrate similar T cell activation capacity.

claim: Murine B-pDCs represent a phenotypically and functionally distinct CLP-derived DC lineage specialized in T cell activation.
source: Murine B-pDCs therefore represent a phenotypically and functionally distinct CLP-derived DC lineage specialized in T cell activation and previously not described in mice.
evidence: Multiple lines of evidence including lineage tracing, gene expression profiling, and functional assays demonstrate this specialization.

claim: B-pDCs have not been previously described in mice.
source: Murine B-pDCs therefore represent a phenotypically and functionally distinct CLP-derived DC lineage specialized in T cell activation and previously not described in mice.
evidence: The authors state this is a novel finding throughout the manuscript.

claim: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) specialize in the production of type I interferons (IFNs).
source: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) specialize in the production of type I interferons (IFNs) and promote antiviral immune responses following engagement of pattern recognition receptors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about pDCs cited in the introduction.

claim: pDCs promote antiviral immune responses following engagement of pattern recognition receptors.
source: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) specialize in the production of type I interferons (IFNs) and promote antiviral immune responses following engagement of pattern recognition receptors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about pDC function.

claim: pDCs have been mainly implicated in the pathogenesis of autoimmune diseases that are characterized by a type I IFN signature (notably, IFN-α).
source: They have been mainly implicated in the pathogenesis of autoimmune diseases that are characterized by a type I IFN signature (notably, IFN-α).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations in the introduction (Di Domizio and Cao, 2013; Swiecki and Colonna, 2015; Sisirak et al., 2014; Rönnblom and Pascual, 2008).

claim: pDCs have been shown to be able to induce tolerogenic immune responses.
source: Yet, pDCs have also been shown to be able to induce tolerogenic immune responses (Di Domizio and Cao, 2013; Swiecki and Colonna, 2015; Sisirak et al., 2014; Rönnblom and Pascual, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: Transcription factor 4 (TCF4) is required for pDC development and for lineage identity.
source: The transcription factor 4 (TCF4) is required for pDC development and for lineage identity (Cisse et al., 2008; Ghosh et al., 2010; Reizis et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: TCF4 is a component of a multiprotein complex that includes both positive and negative regulators.
source: TCF4 is a component of a multiprotein complex that includes both positive and negative regulators (Swiecki and Colonna, 2015; Grajkowska et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: The transcription factor BCL11a is essential for B cell development.
source: One of these components, the transcription factor BCL11a, which is also essential for B cell development (Liu et al., 2003; Ippolito et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2012), induces Tcf4 transcription and initiates a positive feedback loop with TCF4 to maintain pDC lineage commitment and function (Ippolito et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: BCL11a induces Tcf4 transcription and initiates a positive feedback loop with TCF4 to maintain pDC lineage commitment and function.
source: One of these components, the transcription factor BCL11a, which is also essential for B cell development (Liu et al., 2003; Ippolito et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2012), induces Tcf4 transcription and initiates a positive feedback loop with TCF4 to maintain pDC lineage commitment and function (Ippolito et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: pDCs express transcriptional regulators and markers associated with B-lymphocyte development in addition to BCL11a (e.g. B220, SPIB).
source: Unlike their conventional dendritic cell (cDC) counterparts, pDCs express transcriptional regulators and markers associated with B-lymphocyte development in addition to BCL11a (e.g. B220, SPIB) (Pelayo et al., 2005; Sathe et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: pDCs can be generated from myeloid restricted precursors.
source: These features, along with the established generation of pDCs from myeloid restricted precursors (Feng et al., 2022; Harman et al., 2006), have made it difficult to define pDC lineage affiliation (Reizis et al., 2011; Pelayo et al., 2005; Shigematsu et al., 2004; Wang and Liu, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: The dual origin of pDCs from both lymphoid and myeloid progenitors has made it difficult to define pDC lineage affiliation.
source: These features, along with the established generation of pDCs from myeloid restricted precursors (Feng et al., 2022; Harman et al., 2006), have made it difficult to define pDC lineage affiliation (Reizis et al., 2011; Pelayo et al., 2005; Shigematsu et al., 2004; Wang and Liu, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references and represents a synthesis of prior work.

claim: pDC subsets may have distinct origins derived from either the common lymphoid progenitor (CLP) or the common myeloid progenitor (CMP).
source: This has led to the hypothesis that pDC subsets may have distinct origins derived from either the common lymphoid progenitor (CLP) or the common myeloid progenitor (CMP) (Sathe et al., 2013; Nikolic et al., 2002).
evidence: This hypothesis is supported by the cited references.

claim: pDCs with different functional attributes (e.g. variable IFN-α expression levels) have been identified.
source: Beyond the complex nature of their lineage, pDCs with different functional attributes (e.g. variable IFN-α expression levels) or different surface markers (e.g. CD19+ pDCs detected in tumor-draining lymph nodes) have also been identified (Pelayo et al., 2005; Yang et al., 2005; Mellor et al., 2005; Munn et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: CD19+ pDCs have been detected in tumor-draining lymph nodes.
source: Beyond the complex nature of their lineage, pDCs with different functional attributes (e.g. variable IFN-α expression levels) or different surface markers (e.g. CD19+ pDCs detected in tumor-draining lymph nodes) have also been identified (Pelayo et al., 2005; Yang et al., 2005; Mellor et al., 2005; Munn et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: A novel AXL+ dendritic cell (DC) population with many pDC-like properties has been discovered in human blood.
source: On par with the ever-increasing heterogeneity described within pDC populations, a novel AXL+ dendritic cell (DC) population with many pDC-like properties has recently been discovered in human blood (Villani et al., 2017; Alcántara-Hernández et al., 2017; Matsui et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: AXL+ DCs express many canonical pDC protein markers (e.g. CD123, BDCA2/CD303).
source: While AXL+ DCs express many canonical pDC protein markers (e.g. CD123, BDCA2/CD303), they also express CD2, the Ig-like lectins SIGLEC1 and SIGLEC6, as well as the activation marker CD81 (Villani et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference.

claim: AXL+ DCs express CD2, the Ig-like lectins SIGLEC1 and SIGLEC6, as well as the activation marker CD81.
source: While AXL+ DCs express many canonical pDC protein markers (e.g. CD123, BDCA2/CD303), they also express CD2, the Ig-like lectins SIGLEC1 and SIGLEC6, as well as the activation marker CD81 (Villani et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference.

claim: A population of pDCs expressing high levels of CD5 and CD81 has been identified in mice and humans.
source: In a separate study (Zhang et al., 2017), a similar population of pDCs was shown to express high levels of CD5 and CD81 in mice and humans, two glycoproteins normally associated with the B cell receptor (BCR) signaling complex.
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference.

claim: CD5 and CD81 are glycoproteins normally associated with the B cell receptor (BCR) signaling complex.
source: In a separate study (Zhang et al., 2017), a similar population of pDCs was shown to express high levels of CD5 and CD81 in mice and humans, two glycoproteins normally associated with the B cell receptor (BCR) signaling complex.
evidence: This is established knowledge about BCR signaling components.

claim: The origin of AXL+ transitional DCs is currently unclear.
source: The origin of AXL+ transitional DCs is currently unclear and the presence of a homologous population in mice remains muddled.
evidence: This represents the state of knowledge prior to the current study.

claim: The presence of a homologous population to human AXL+ DCs in mice remains muddled.
source: The origin of AXL+ transitional DCs is currently unclear and the presence of a homologous population in mice remains muddled.
evidence: This represents the state of knowledge prior to the current study.

claim: Conditional deletion of Bcl11a in the hematopoietic stem cell compartment mediated by Vav1-Cre results in complete abolishment of pDC development.
source: We previously demonstrated that conditional deletion of Bcl11a in the hematopoietic stem cell compartment mediated by Vav1-Cre or by inducible Mx1-Cre recombinase results in complete abolishment of pDC development (Ippolito et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference to prior work by the authors.

claim: Conditional deletion of Bcl11a in the hematopoietic stem cell compartment mediated by inducible Mx1-Cre recombinase results in complete abolishment of pDC development.
source: We previously demonstrated that conditional deletion of Bcl11a in the hematopoietic stem cell compartment mediated by Vav1-Cre or by inducible Mx1-Cre recombinase results in complete abolishment of pDC development (Ippolito et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference to prior work by the authors.

claim: Expression of the Cd79a gene initiates at the LY6D+ CLP stage, in B-cell-biased lymphoid progenitors (BLPs).
source: Expression of the Cd79a gene (Cd79a) initiates at the LY6D+ CLP stage, in B-cell-biased lymphoid progenitors (BLPs) (Inlay et al., 2009), downstream of LY6D– CLPs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference and confirmed by YFP expression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: BLPs are downstream of LY6D– CLPs.
source: Expression of the Cd79a gene (Cd79a) initiates at the LY6D+ CLP stage, in B-cell-biased lymphoid progenitors (BLPs) (Inlay et al., 2009), downstream of LY6D– CLPs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: B220+ PDCA1+ pDCs were consistently and significantly reduced by an average of ~25% (24.8 ± 2.4%) in Bcl11aF/FCd79a-Cre mice relative to littermates.
source: B220+ PDCA1+ pDCs (all found to be CD11c int) were consistently and significantly reduced by an average of ~25% (24.8 ± 2.4%) in cKO mice relative to littermates (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: All B220+ PDCA1+ pDCs are CD11c int.
source: B220+ PDCA1+ pDCs (all found to be CD11c int) were consistently and significantly reduced by an average of ~25% (24.8 ± 2.4%) in cKO mice relative to littermates (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the flow cytometry analysis.

claim: A significant proportion of pDCs are derived from BLPs or BLP-derived cells.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that a significant proportion of pDCs are derived from BLPs or BLP-derived cells and are Bcl11a dependent.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the conditional deletion experiments showing ~25% reduction in pDCs.

claim: BLP-derived pDCs are Bcl11a dependent.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that a significant proportion of pDCs are derived from BLPs or BLP-derived cells and are Bcl11a dependent.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the reduction in pDCs upon Bcl11a deletion in Cd79a+ cells.

claim: Less than 10% of B cells (B220+ PDCA1-) in the spleens of Cd79a-Cre-YFP recipients were YFP–, confirming elimination of recipient hematopoiesis.
source: After 8 weeks, <10% of B cells (B220+ PDCA1-) in the spleens of Cd79a-Cre-YFP recipients were YFP–, confirming elimination of recipient hematopoiesis (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 1D and E from bone marrow transplantation experiments.

claim: Bcl11aF/FCd79a-Cre-YFP BM resulted in significantly reduced B cell and pDC cellularity compared to Cd79a-Cre-YFP controls.
source: As expected, Bcl11aF/FCd79a-Cre-YFP BM resulted in significantly reduced B cell and pDC cellularity compared to Cd79a-Cre-YFP controls, whereas BCL11A-sufficient (YFP–) pDCs persisted (Figure 1C, E, and F).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C, E, and F from bone marrow transplantation experiments.

claim: BCL11A-sufficient (YFP–) pDCs persisted in Bcl11aF/FCd79a-Cre-YFP BM transplant recipients.
source: As expected, Bcl11aF/FCd79a-Cre-YFP BM resulted in significantly reduced B cell and pDC cellularity compared to Cd79a-Cre-YFP controls, whereas BCL11A-sufficient (YFP–) pDCs persisted (Figure 1C, E, and F).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C, E, and F.

claim: Approximately one-third of pDCs in the spleen of wildtype chimeras were YFP+ compared to only one-fifth in BM.
source: Approximately one-third of pDCs in the spleen of wildtype chimeras were YFP+ compared to only one-fifth in BM (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is shown by quantification in Figure 1G.

claim: BLP-derived pDCs preferentially home to the spleen.
source: This increased fraction of YFP+ pDCs in the spleen suggests that BLP-derived pDCs preferentially home to that organ.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential distribution of YFP+ pDCs between spleen and bone marrow.

claim: Cd79a-cre expression occurs subsequent to T-B lineage divergence.
source: This indicated that Cd79a-cre expression occurs subsequent to T-B lineage divergence, consonant with the previous observations (Inlay et al., 2009; Nagaharu et al., 2022; Herman and Grün, 2018) and our Cd79a-cre progenitor analysis in which YFP+ cells are confined to the BLP-derived compartment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by cited references and confirmed by YFP expression analysis in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: YFP+ cells are confined to the BLP-derived compartment.
source: This indicated that Cd79a-cre expression occurs subsequent to T-B lineage divergence, consonant with the previous observations (Inlay et al., 2009; Nagaharu et al., 2022; Herman and Grün, 2018) and our Cd79a-cre progenitor analysis in which YFP+ cells are confined to the BLP-derived compartment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry analysis in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Resting B-pDCs express higher levels of MHC Class II relative to Cd79a- pDCs.
source: Relative to Cd79a- pDCs, resting B-pDCs express higher levels of MHC Class II (Figure 2A and B), suggesting that they may be primed for immediate response to pro-inflammatory signals.
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 2A and B.

claim: B-pDCs may be primed for immediate response to pro-inflammatory signals.
source: Relative to Cd79a- pDCs, resting B-pDCs express higher levels of MHC Class II (Figure 2A and B), suggesting that they may be primed for immediate response to pro-inflammatory signals.
evidence: This is inferred from the higher MHC Class II expression.

claim: Both pDC and B-pDC compartments expanded relative to controls 24 hr after TLR9 ligand (CpG:ODN) injection.
source: To test this hypothesis, we delivered TLR9 ligand (CpG:ODN) into Cd79a-Cre-YFP mice via tail vein injection, and splenic pDCs were phenotyped via flow cytometry 24 hr later. While both pDC and B-pDC compartments expanded relative to controls (Figure 2C and D), the YFP+ B-pDC fraction increased almost twofold above that of the YFP– pDC fraction in numbers (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The YFP+ B-pDC fraction increased almost twofold above that of the YFP– pDC fraction in numbers after CpG:ODN injection.
source: While both pDC and B-pDC compartments expanded relative to controls (Figure 2C and D), the YFP+ B-pDC fraction increased almost twofold above that of the YFP– pDC fraction in numbers (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is shown by quantification in Figure 2E.

claim: Fold increase of B-pDCs coexpressing CD83 and CD86 upon activation was significantly higher than that of YFP- pDCs.
source: Additionally, fold increase of B-pDCs coexpressing CD83 and CD86 upon activation was also significantly higher than that of YFP- pDCs (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 2F and G.

claim: B-pDCs are intrinsically activated and primed for rapid expansion upon TLR9 engagement relative to YFP- pDCs.
source: These results suggested that relative to YFP- pDCs, B-pDCs are intrinsically activated and primed for rapid expansion upon TLR9 engagement.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the expansion and activation marker data.

claim: IFN-α production was almost negligible in B-pDC.
source: IFN-α production was almost negligible in B-pDC (Figure 2H), yet IL-12p40 production was significantly augmented over pDC (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is shown by ELISA data in Figure 2H.

claim: IL-12p40 production was significantly augmented in B-pDCs over pDCs.
source: IFN-α production was almost negligible in B-pDC (Figure 2H), yet IL-12p40 production was significantly augmented over pDC (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is shown by ELISA data in Figure 2H.

claim: B-pDCs were significantly better at expanding T cells in co-cultures than conventional pDCs upon TLR9 activation.
source: Altogether, our results showed B-pDCs were significantly better at expanding T cells in co-cultures than conventional pDCs (Figure 2I and J) upon TLR9 activation.
evidence: This is shown by co-culture experiments in Figure 2I and J.

claim: Approximately 1% of transcripts (~220 genes) differed significantly (q-value<0.05) between B-pDCs and classical pDCs.
source: While the overall gene expression patterns were highly similar across the two subsets,~1% of transcripts (~220 genes) differed significantly (q-value<0.05) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq analysis in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Among the top overexpressed genes in B-pDCs were Lyz1, Ccr3, Cd86, Id2, Axl, Siglec1, and Cd81.
source: Among the top overexpressed genes in B-pDCs were Lyz1, Ccr3, Cd86, Id2, Axl, Siglec1, and Cd81 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq analysis in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Differentially expressed transcripts between B-pDCs and pDCs generated Gene Ontology (GO) terms including 'immune response', 'inflammatory response', 'cell activation', and 'regulation of immune response'.
source: Differentially expressed transcripts generated Gene Ontology (GO) (Huang et al., 2009) or Panther (Thomas et al., 2003) terms including 'immune response', 'inflammatory response', 'cell activation', and 'regulation of immune response' (p=1.36 × 10–17, 2.15×10–12, 3.67×10–11, and 1.45×10–10), respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by GO analysis in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: pDCs and B-pDCs expression levels were strongly correlated with one another relative to early B cells (R2 values = 0.8959, 0.4145, and 0.404, respectively).
source: As shown in Figure 2D, pDCs and B-pDCs expression levels were strongly correlated with one another relative to early B cells (R2 values = 0.8959, 0.4145, and 0.404, respectively) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by correlation analysis in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: B-pDCs are functionally distinct from classical pDCs and specialize in inflammatory responses, antigen presentation, and T cell activation.
source: Collectively, these data support our contention that B-pDCs are functionally distinct from classical pDCs and specialize in inflammatory responses, antigen presentation, and T cell activation.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from multiple lines of evidence including gene expression, cytokine production, and T cell co-culture experiments.

claim: AXL+ transitional DCs (tDCs or AS-DCs) have been identified in humans by the high expression levels of the genes AXL, CD81, CD86, LYZ2, C1QA, CD2, and C1QB relative to classical pDCs.
source: AXL+ transitional DCs (tDCs or AS-DCs) Villani et al., 2017; Leylek et al., 2019 have been identified in humans by the high expression levels of the genes AXL, CD81, CD86, LYZ2, C1QA, CD2, and C1QB relative to classical pDCs (Villani et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017; Alcántara-Hernández et al., 2017; Matsui et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: Human AXL+ transitional DCs exhibit many classical pDC features and have been described phenotypically as a 'continuum' between pDC and cDC2 populations.
source: They also exhibit many classical pDC features, having previously been described phenotypically as a 'continuum' between pDC and cDC2 populations (Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference.

claim: More than 95% of B220+ PDCA1- cells were CD19+ SIGLEC-H- (B cells).
source: As expected, B220+ PDCA1- cells were >95% CD19+ SIGLEC-H- (B cells).
evidence: This is shown by imaging flow cytometry in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: More than 95% of B220+ PDCA1 hi cells were SIGLEC-H +and CD19-.
source: Most importantly, >95% of B220+ PDCA1 hi cells were SIGLEC-H +and CD19-, ruling out any pDC population contamination (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by imaging flow cytometry in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Approximately 60% of B-pDCs were positive for AXL.
source: At the protein level, we were able to stain mouse BM cells with anti-AXL antibodies without issues and confirmed that while ~60% of B-pDCs were positive for AXL, only ~10% of YFP negative pDCs expressed this protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by imaging flow cytometry in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Only approximately 10% of YFP negative pDCs expressed AXL protein.
source: At the protein level, we were able to stain mouse BM cells with anti-AXL antibodies without issues and confirmed that while ~60% of B-pDCs were positive for AXL, only ~10% of YFP negative pDCs expressed this protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by imaging flow cytometry in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: B-pDCs resembled classical secretory pDCs morphologically, presenting a large nucleus and defined plasma-like features, in contrast to B cells.
source: Finally, imaging of BM cells showed that B-pDCs resembled classical secretory pDCs morphologically, presenting a large nucleus and defined plasma-like features, in contrast to B cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by imaging flow cytometry in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: B-pDCs might prioritize their secretory capacity for copious transcription and secretion of alternative immune system modulators.
source: This preliminary phenotypic analysis led us to speculate that similarly to human AXL+ transitional DCs, B-pDC might also prioritize their secretory capacity for copious transcription and secretion of alternative immune system modulators.
evidence: This is speculation based on morphological and functional similarities to human AXL+ DCs.

claim: Principal component-based clustering and UMAP visualization of sorted PDCA+ cells yielded 22 discrete clusters.
source: Principal component-based clustering and UMAP visualization of sorted PDCA+ cells yielded 22 discrete clusters.
evidence: This is shown by single-cell RNA-seq analysis in Figure 3.

claim: PDCA1+ cells comprised nine distinct pDC populations (including B-pDCs).
source: PDCA1+ cells comprised nine distinct pDC populations (including B-pDCs, which were unanimously classified as pDCs by CIPR identity scores despite its unique Cd79a expression).
evidence: This is shown by single-cell RNA-seq analysis and CIPR classification.

claim: B-pDCs were unanimously classified as pDCs by CIPR identity scores despite their unique Cd79a expression.
source: PDCA1+ cells comprised nine distinct pDC populations (including B-pDCs, which were unanimously classified as pDCs by CIPR identity scores despite its unique Cd79a expression).
evidence: This is shown by CIPR analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: Except for Cd79a and Cd79b, B-pDCs showed negligible expression of mature B cell associated genes such as Pax5, Cd19, and Cd22.
source: Except for Cd79a and Cd79b, B-pDCs showed negligible expression of mature B cell associated genes such as Pax5, Cd19, and Cd22 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is shown by single-cell RNA-seq analysis in Figure 3C.

claim: Expression of canonical pDC genes was present but reduced in B-pDCs relative to classical pDC subsets.
source: Expression of canonical pDC genes was present but reduced in B-pDCs relative to classical pDC subsets (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is shown by single-cell RNA-seq analysis in Figure 3D.

claim: B-pDCs are not a direct precursor for B cells based on their single-cell developmental trajectory.
source: Although we cannot say the pre/pro B cell-like Prog1 cluster represents an immediately adjacent common progenitor for B cells and B-pDCs, we confirmed B-pDCs are not a direct precursor for B cells based on their single-cell developmental trajectory.
evidence: This is shown by pseudotime analysis in Figure 4.

claim: B-pDCs retained expression of early BCR associated genes, including Ly6d, Ighm, Igkc, Iglc2, and Jchain.
source: Although B-pDCs did not express detectable levels of most B cell commitment markers evaluated, they did retain expression of early BCR associated genes, including Ly6d, Ighm, Igkc, Iglc2, and Jchain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by pseudotime analysis in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: B-pDCs express negligible levels of TACI.
source: We discovered that B-pDCs express negligible levels of TACI (a transcription factor that silences the B cell developmental program; Shapiro-Shelef and Calame, 2005), and that expression of CD138 and IgG1 was also negligible (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and not shown), thus ruling out any major plasma cell overlap at the protein level.
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: B-pDCs express negligible levels of CD138 and IgG1.
source: We discovered that B-pDCs express negligible levels of TACI (a transcription factor that silences the B cell developmental program; Shapiro-Shelef and Calame, 2005), and that expression of CD138 and IgG1 was also negligible (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and not shown), thus ruling out any major plasma cell overlap at the protein level.
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: TACI is a transcription factor that silences the B cell developmental program.
source: We discovered that B-pDCs express negligible levels of TACI (a transcription factor that silences the B cell developmental program; Shapiro-Shelef and Calame, 2005), and that expression of CD138 and IgG1 was also negligible (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and not shown), thus ruling out any major plasma cell overlap at the protein level.
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference.

claim: B-pDCs enhanced expression of the pDC associated markers Siglech, Tcf4, Bst2, and Xbp1 as they develop.
source: Lineage analysis also revealed that B-pDCs enhanced expression of the pDC associated markers Siglech, Tcf4, Bst2, and also of Xbp1 (a marker expressed at high levels in secretory cells).
evidence: This is shown by pseudotime analysis in Figure 4D.

claim: Xbp1 is a marker expressed at high levels in secretory cells.
source: Lineage analysis also revealed that B-pDCs enhanced expression of the pDC associated markers Siglech, Tcf4, Bst2, and also of Xbp1 (a marker expressed at high levels in secretory cells).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Xbp1 function.

claim: Committed B cells downregulated pDC associated markers as they progressed through pseudotime.
source: Committed B cells in turn downregulated these markers as they progressed through pseudotime (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is shown by pseudotime analysis in Figure 4D.

claim: As B-pDCs develop, they retain expression of both early BCR genes and pDC associated genes, diverging from B cells through continued suppression of transcription factors required for terminal B cell differentiation.
source: In summary, lineage analyses revealed that as B-pDCs develop, they retain expression of both early BCR genes and pDC associated genes, diverging from B cells through continued suppression of transcription factors required for terminal B cell differentiation.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: B-pDCs and pDC5 are identified as 'noncanonical pDCs' due to their distinguishing high expression of Axl.
source: We identified B-pDCs and pDC5 as 'noncanonical pDCs' due to their distinguishing high expression of Axl (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown by single-cell RNA-seq analysis in Figure 5A.

claim: Lyz2, the complement genes C1qa, C1qb, C1qc, and Cd5l were the top conserved markers for B-pDCs and pDC5s.
source: We then analyzed the top DEGs shared between B-pDCs and pDC5s using the function 'FindConservedMarkers'. Lyz2, the complement genes C1qa, C1qb, C1qc, and Cd5l, were the top conserved markers for these two pDC subsets (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown by single-cell RNA-seq analysis in Figure 5A.

claim: Cd5l is a macrophage associated secreted protein that has been shown to play a major role in initiating inflammation and maintaining humoral responses.
source: Of note, Cd5l, a macrophage associated secreted protein, has been shown to play a major role in initiating inflammation and maintaining humoral responses (Sanjurjo et al., 2015; Martinez et al., 2014; Oskam et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: Constitutive expression of Axl and innate activation markers are present in more than one transcriptionally distinct murine pDC profile.
source: Altogether, our analysis revealed that constitutive expression of Axl and innate activation markers are present in more than one transcriptionally distinct murine pDC profile, stressing the functional heterogeneity and plasticity of murine pDCs.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the identification of both B-pDCs and pDC5 as Axl+ populations.

claim: Noncanonical AXL+ DCs in humans have been shown to be derived from a myeloid pro-pDC progenitor.
source: Noncanonical AXL+ DCs in humans have been shown to be derived from a myeloid pro-pDC progenitor (Dress et al., 2019; Herman and Grün, 2018; Rodrigues et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: B-pDCs were not developmentally linked to 'classical' AXL negative pDCs or Axl+ pDC5 cells.
source: Ultimately, this statistical grouping confirmed that B-pDCs were not developmentally linked to 'classical' AXL negative pDCs or Axl+ pDC5 cells.
evidence: This is shown by Monocle3 trajectory analysis in Figure 5B.

claim: B-pDCs did not integrate into the predicted lineage trajectory originating from Prog2.
source: Accordingly, B-pDCs did not integrate into the predicted lineage trajectory originating from Prog2, whereas the Axl+ pDC5 population did (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown by Monocle3 trajectory analysis in Figure 5B.

claim: The Axl+ pDC5 population integrated into the predicted lineage trajectory originating from Prog2.
source: Accordingly, B-pDCs did not integrate into the predicted lineage trajectory originating from Prog2, whereas the Axl+ pDC5 population did (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown by Monocle3 trajectory analysis in Figure 5B.

claim: Both B-pDCs and pDC5s exhibited a similar late developmental pseudotime.
source: Both B-pDCs and pDC5s exhibited a similar late developmental pseudotime, while clusters pDC6 and pDC4 were the first to develop from Prog2.
evidence: This is shown by pseudotime analysis in Figure 5B.

claim: Clusters pDC6 and pDC4 were the first to develop from Prog2.
source: Both B-pDCs and pDC5s exhibited a similar late developmental pseudotime, while clusters pDC6 and pDC4 were the first to develop from Prog2.
evidence: This is shown by pseudotime analysis in Figure 5B.

claim: Murine noncanonical pDCs (AXL+) consist of at least two major pDC subpopulations, which develop from lymphoid and myeloid progenitors, respectively.
source: Collectively, our data establish that murine noncanonical pDCs (AXL+) consist of at least two major pDC subpopulations, which develop from lymphoid and myeloid progenitors, respectively.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from lineage tracing and trajectory analysis showing B-pDCs derive from lymphoid progenitors while pDC5 derives from myeloid progenitors.

claim: The murine pDC compartment is bipartite, being comprised of B-pDCs—diverted from the CLP post T-B bifurcation—as well as myeloid-derived classical pDCs.
source: Our data shows that the murine pDC compartment is bipartite, being comprised of B-pDCs—diverted from the CLP post T-B bifurcation—as well as myeloid-derived classical pDCs.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the lineage tracing and developmental trajectory analyses.

claim: B-pDCs constitutively express high levels of multiple innate activation markers, including C1qa, C1qb, Lyz2, and Cd81.
source: Unlike most myeloid-derived pDCs, B-pDCs constitutively express high levels of multiple innate activation markers, including C1qa, C1qb, Lyz2, and Cd81.
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq analyses.

claim: B-pDCs expand more readily after TLR9 engagement than classical pDCs.
source: Functionally, they expand more readily after TLR9 engagement than classical pDCs (either through increased proliferation or differentiation of other cell types) and excel at activating T cells in culture.
evidence: This is shown by in vivo CpG stimulation experiments in Figure 2.

claim: B-pDCs excel at activating T cells in culture.
source: Functionally, they expand more readily after TLR9 engagement than classical pDCs (either through increased proliferation or differentiation of other cell types) and excel at activating T cells in culture.
evidence: This is shown by co-culture experiments in Figure 2I and J.

claim: B-pDCs comprise almost one-fifth of the total pDC compartment.
source: While further functional definition awaits discovery, our work provides a framework for the identification and segregation of the B-pDC lineage (comprising almost one-fifth of the total pDC compartment) from other myeloid-derived pDC subpopulations.
evidence: This is inferred from the ~25% reduction in pDCs upon Bcl11a deletion in Cd79a+ cells and the distribution of YFP+ pDCs in chimeras.

claim: DC functionality derives primarily from ontogeny rather than from tissue environment.
source: Primarily, our observations support the hypothesis that DC functionality derives primarily from ontogeny rather than from tissue environment (Heidkamp et al., 2016), exemplified by evolution of a specialized pDC lineage from a lymphoid progenitor.
evidence: This hypothesis is supported by the cited reference and the authors' findings.

claim: B-pDCs may deviate from B cell commitment after Ly6d expression.
source: In the case of the B-pDCs, our data suggest such a cell may deviate from B cell commitment after Ly6d expression, thought to be the earliest marker of B cell specification (Inlay et al., 2009).
evidence: This is inferred from the timing of Cd79a expression and the developmental trajectory analysis, supported by the cited reference.

claim: Ly6d is thought to be the earliest marker of B cell specification.
source: In the case of the B-pDCs, our data suggest such a cell may deviate from B cell commitment after Ly6d expression, thought to be the earliest marker of B cell specification (Inlay et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference.

claim: Ablation of AXL in mice has been shown to increase expression of type I IFN while impairing IL-1β production and T cell activation during viral infections.
source: Of note, ablation of AXL in mice has previously been shown to increase expression of type I IFN while impairing IL-1β production and T cell activation during viral infections (Schmid et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claim: AXL+ B-pDCs may play an important role in advancing T cell expansion, while curbing innate immune responses that can result in autoimmune damage.
source: Our related findings that AXL+ B-pDCs excel at T cell priming but exhibit reduced IFNα expression might suggest these DCs play an important role in advancing T cell expansion, while curbing innate immune responses that can result in autoimmune damage.
evidence: This is speculation based on the functional characteristics of B-pDCs and known effects of AXL.

claim: Murine pDCs can develop in parallel from either myeloid or lymphoid progenitors.
source: In addition to describing a novel B cell-like pDC population, we profiled murine can develop in parallel from either myeloid or lymphoid progenitors, with lymphoid-derived B-pDCs retaining expression of additional early B cell genes that are not expressed in myeloid-derived pDCs.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the lineage tracing and trajectory analyses.

claim: Lymphoid-derived B-pDCs retain expression of additional early B cell genes that are not expressed in myeloid-derived pDCs.
source: In addition to describing a novel B cell-like pDC population, we profiled murine can develop in parallel from either myeloid or lymphoid progenitors, with lymphoid-derived B-pDCs retaining expression of additional early B cell genes that are not expressed in myeloid-derived pDCs.
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq analyses showing B-pDCs express Cd79a, Cd79b, and early BCR genes.

claim: The demarcation of lymphoid derived B-pDCs as one of the AXL+ pDC populations found in mice may help clarify the perceived plasticity of the pDC compartment in normal and disease contexts.
source: The demarcation of lymphoid derived B-pDCs as one of the AXL+ pDC populations found in mice may help clarify the perceived plasticity of the pDC compartment in normal and disease contexts (Li et al., 2017), as well as provide a new cell for targeted study within the context of autoimmune disease, cancer, and infection models.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential impact of the findings, supported by a citation.

claim: B-pDCs may provide a new cell for targeted study within the context of autoimmune disease, cancer, and infection models.
source: The demarcation of lymphoid derived B-pDCs as one of the AXL+ pDC populations found in mice may help clarify the perceived plasticity of the pDC compartment in normal and disease contexts (Li et al., 2017), as well as provide a new cell for targeted study within the context of autoimmune disease, cancer, and infection models.
evidence: This is speculation about potential future research applications.
